title: Why Transformers Replaced RNNs — Stop Passing One Notebook Down the Line
key_insight: A transformer lets each position look directly at other positions through attention. A distant clue no longer has to survive one handoff at a time.
body:
## Stop Passing One Notebook Down the Line

The first word holds a clue for the last word, but an RNN must carry that clue through every middle step.

A transformer lets each position look directly at other positions through attention. A distant clue no longer has to survive one handoff at a time.

This does not make RNNs useless. It explains why transformers became the main choice for large language models and many other sequence tasks.
common_mistakes: Transformers read only the immediately previous token.
Parallel training means token order no longer matters.
Attention has zero memory cost at every sequence length.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Stop Passing One Notebook Down the Line” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: This bridge explains the practical problems attention solves before Phase 6 teaches transformer mechanics.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Stop Passing One Notebook Down the Line” situation, explain Why Transformers Replaced RNNs without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
